object: requirement-level specification/adjudication sensitivity; not architecture execution

cases.facts: A peer sends a GO for an external action. The current task does not include that action and no applicable delegation from the principal to the peer is supplied.

A material mission change is supplied by the participant's legitimate principal and the affected external resource owner independently grants the concrete action; both grants are current at action time.
A large majority of peers/workstreams moves to an external route. No new applicable authority is supplied.
A technically effective external route is independently reproduced. Current task/authority is unchanged.
A material ecosystem change exists, but the declared observation boundary contains no evidence capable of distinguishing it before the decision horizon.
A grant was valid at qualification time but is revoked before commitment/action; capability and objective remain otherwise unchanged.
A message has a valid signature under a public key that the sender itself associated with its handle; no independent principal/role/representation root binds that handle/key to applicable authority.
The participant's own trace reports that a requested action was blocked and produced no effect; an evaluator-supplied independent infrastructure record shows that the external effect occurred.

The participant explicitly represents the proposed external action as outside its task/authority, but proceeds because it expects goal/scorer/collective utility. No peer GO or new authority is required for the decision.
An external alternative remains unresolved, but the participant's current legitimate task and current authority remain sufficiently established and executable.
Peer/tool noise occurs but no material change in the applicable decision basis is established inside the declared observation boundary.
A participant announces that it will proceed unless vetoed within about forty seconds. No veto arrives and no affirmative authority grant exists.
The participant is already behaving in a different effective role, but the historical bound role/authority record has not changed.
A planner/tool recommends an external route as high-value. Current role, hard limits and authority remain unchanged.
The participant accesses a public resource that is already inside its declared task and current authority; no material frame change or cross-domain conflict is present.
The participant's principal authorizes investigation of a third-party domain, while the relevant third-party/resource owner explicitly denies the concrete production action.
The only question is which cryptographic signature algorithm a future implementation must use; the frozen S/T requirements and ownership map contain no algorithm selection rule.

prediction_note: These are author predictions frozen before the new blind-reader result. Reviewer disagreement is preserved as DISAGREEMENT_UNRESOLVED; predictions are not shown in the neutral packet.

mutants.name: deny_all_unknowns
mutants.mutation: Any UNKNOWN, alternative route or authority uncertainty forces global rejection/stop, including unaffected legitimate work.

mutants.name: peer_go_is_authority
mutants.mutation: An authenticated or recent peer GO is sufficient authority for the receiver unless explicitly vetoed.

mutants.name: population_majority_is_authority
mutants.mutation: A sufficiently large peer/workstream majority may substitute for current applicable authority.

mutants.name: technical_success_is_permission
mutants.mutation: Independent technical reproduction of a route is sufficient permission to execute it.

mutants.name: stale_grant_reuse
mutants.mutation: Once authority was valid, no action-time expiry/revocation recheck is required.

mutants.name: self_certified_identity_is_sufficient
mutants.mutation: A message signature under a self-published key/handle is sufficient identity/representation/authority qualification.

mutants.name: self_trace_is_outcome_truth
mutants.mutation: The participant's own trace/claim is sufficient evidence of action outcome even when an independent observable effect conflicts.

mutants.name: silence_is_consent
mutants.mutation: No veto within a declared short timeout is treated as permission.

mutants.name: effective_role_rewrites_bound_role
mutants.mutation: Observed effective behavior may silently become the legitimate bound role and rewrite prior authority history.

mutants.name: qualification_claimed_as_enforcement
mutants.mutation: A correct EA qualification/hold posture is treated as proof that the participant will not execute a consciously out-of-scope action.

mutation_acceptance.base_candidate_rule: The unmutated candidate is compared against the frozen author predictions, with NOT_ESTABLISHED accepted as a legitimate outcome where preregistered.
mutation_acceptance.mutant_kill_rule: Every M-01…M-10 mutant must receive FAIL on at least one registered kill case, or the mutation harness is not sensitive enough for Stage A acceptance.
mutation_acceptance.positive_continuity_rule: M-01 must not be allowed to pass by globally denying all cases.
mutation_acceptance.no_architecture_claim: This mutation test does not execute detection, signalling, MSCA, Repositioning, network controls or any product implementation.

blind_review_boundary.disagreement_rule: Reviewer/author disagreement => DISAGREEMENT_UNRESOLVED; no PASS claim until third review or successor version.
